thread:
maria: post-RFC sanity check — noticed a latency bump on FA v3 vs v2 for mid-length seqs (256-1024). p95 up ~15-20% across a small sample set on A100. anyone else seeing this?
kevin: yep saw that in the nightly perf graph. p50 fine, p95 regressed. throughput unchanged.
sanjay: sharing numbers: v2 p95=84ms, v3 p95=101ms for seq=512 batch=4 (A100), model=gpt-medium-compat. logs attached in prism.
maria: thanks. important: this is after we switched default kernel selection to prefer v3 for seq>128 in the router RFC. suspect either kernel micro-op differences or workspace alloc pattern.
lee: quick hypothesis: v3 has slightly different workspace fragmentation that hurts allocator for midseq + small batches. also possible extra memcpy for jagged attention shapes.
toni: also noticed v3 uses an extra prefetch in the attention loop for certain tile sizes. that should reduce tail variance, not increase it, but maybe it interacts with concurrent kernels.
kevin: repro command i used for microbench: `python infra/bench/mini_infer.py --model gpt-medium-compat --seq 512 --batch 4 --kernel flashattn_v3 --reps 300 --profile`. yields the p95 numbers above.
sanjay: ran with --batch 8 and the delta shrinks to ~6%. so it seems batch size interacts strongly.
maria: good signal. can we get perf counters (SM utilization, L2 miss, DRAM bw) for both kernels during the microbench? suspect L2 thrash or extra kernel launches.
lee: i ran nvprof on a couple runs. v3 shows slightly higher global memory transactions and more device-to-device memcpy ops around KV cache handling. paste log: ```
==BEGIN NVPROF SNIPPET==
Kernel flash_attn_v2   time 45.2ms  gmem_reads 1.2e9  l2_loads 3.4e7
Kernel flash_attn_v3   time 51.8ms  gmem_reads 1.5e9  l2_loads 4.1e7
Memcpy D2D             time 2.1ms
==END NVPROF SNIPPET==
```
toni: interesting. v3 has extra gmem reads. could be due to a fallback path for certain head counts or an extra permutation. which model config?
sanjay: heads=16, head_dim=64. no hetero head shapes. single-stream KV cache enabled for the bench.
maria: that D2D memcpy stands out. we don't expect D2D for same-device KV ops. maybe a temp buffer allocation and copy for alignment. can you grep for `cudaMemcpyPeerAsync` in the kernel wrapper?
kevin: looked at the v3 wrapper patch in the RFC branch: there is a small refactor that stages padded workspace into an aligned buffer then memcpy into compact workspace. it was meant to avoid misaligned loads on older archs. maybe alignment path is being triggered unnecessarily.
lee: run with env `FA_V3_FORCE_COMPACT=1` and `FA_V3_ENABLE_PREFETCH=0` to toggle. i tested locally: forcing compact reduces D2D and drops p95 back ~8% (not fully to v2).
maria: useful. can we add telemetry flag to record whether the alignment-copy path triggers in prod so we know how common this is? also need a perf regression label in the rollout dashboard.
toni: agree. i'll open a tiny PR to add a tracepoint when the alignment copy is taken and expose it to runtime telemetry as `fa_v3_align_copy=true/false`.
sanjay: action: kevin to run full sweep across seq lengths [64,128,256,512,1024], batches [1,2,4,8] with both kernels and env toggles, collect nvprof counters; lee to try a patched allocator that returns pre-aligned buffers to avoid copy; toni will add tracepoint + rollout metric.
kevin: i'll kick off the sweep on the perf rig and post results here. ETA ~3 hours. /cc @ops-bot please keep the perf rig reserved during runs.
ops-bot: perf-rig-03 reserved for kevin for 3h starting now. :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks. after results, if alignment-copy is the cause we should either: revert the alignment staging, make it conditional by hw capability, or wire allocation to provide aligned workspace. prefer last two.
lee: also worth checking how this interacts with quantized kernels (int8 path). if the staging is generic it might be adding copies in that path too. i'll include an int8 probe.
toni: note: if we patch allocation we need a small release note — could affect memory accounting in Dedicated. i'll draft a short blurb for release notes.
sanjay: if the delta persists after disabling copying, next suspects: kernel launch config (grid/blocks) and warp-level shuffles. we can diff PTX for hot kernels.
maria: great plan. keep updates here. if anyone finds a quick mitigation that reduces p95 we can enable as hotfix on canary. otherwise put rollback gating on v3 rollout.
kevin: initial sweep started, posting intermediate summary in ~90m.
lee: thanks all. :thumbsup:
